subject.title: Feature Request: Extract text from document attachments in Telegram channel

question: What Office-document extraction scope and security boundary should OpenClaw support for Telegram and shared attachment paths?
rationale: Automation can prove the gap, but choosing parser dependencies, MIME coverage, decompression/XML limits, and whether this belongs in the bundled document-extract plugin requires maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Bounded shared extractor
options.body: Add only maintainer-approved Office MIME types through the shared document-extractor contract with explicit parser limits, tests, and docs.

options.title: External MCP first
options.body: Keep native Office extraction out of core for now and document/publish a ClawHub or MCP companion such as markitdown for users who opt in.

options.title: Provider-native track
options.body: Defer local extraction and solve the broader provider-native file/document input contract first.

recommendation.title: Bounded shared extractor
recommendation.body: Add only maintainer-approved Office MIME types through the shared document-extractor contract with explicit parser limits, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the shared document-extract and input_file seams that would own the bounded implementation.
